answer: A work-based reputation market resists fake identities by tying influence to costly, attested history rather than account creation. Like a canyon carved by a long river, trust deepens only through tasks verified by independent counterparties, with deposits slashed for fraud. On the knoll where newcomers gather, entry requires a refundable bond and capped rewards during probation, so thousands of clones multiply locked capital and waiting time, not power. At the kernel of the design, voting weight follows proven work and stake, not headcount, so free accounts cannot outvote seasoned agents.
